rituals.title: THE ODDS RECEIPT
rituals.goal: Fear speaks in certainty; reality keeps percentages.
rituals.steps:
1. Score Odds — Give the prediction a number from 0 to 100.
2. Check Baseline — Find one real reference point: how often has this happened in similar situations?
3. Weigh Evidence — Notice one fact that raises the odds and another that lowers them.
4. Revise Odds — Pick a new number and remember it.
5. Follow Evidence — Act from the revision, not the original alarm.
rituals.win: ✓ Disaster stopped being the only ending.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Follow Evidence”; leave the forecast.
• Loop back? Use “Weigh Evidence”.
• “Revise Odds” — fear isn’t fate.
• What lost power: “Score Odds” → “Follow Evidence”?
• I can use “Check Baseline” while fear stays loud.
rituals.formula_flow: Score Odds → Check Baseline → Weigh Evidence → Revise Odds → Follow Evidence
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
End the count if numbers become reassurance checking or you cannot stop recalculating.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE BAD VOICE ACTOR
rituals.goal: Authority often hides inside delivery.
rituals.steps:
1. Read Wrong — Hear the thought as a tired GPS, an overdramatic sports commentator, or a hesitant intern reading the wrong memo.
2. Keep Words — Keep the words unchanged; alter only tempo, pitch, and confidence.
3. Replay — Then replay it in your natural voice as a possibility, not an order.
rituals.win: ✓ A fixed rule turned back into a context-dependent idea.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Replay”; loosen the label.
• Shortcut: “Keep Words”, once.
• “Keep Words” — the rule loosened.
• “Read Wrong” versus “Replay”: what eased?
• I can use “Keep Words” without becoming the label.
rituals.formula_flow: Read Wrong → Keep Words → Replay
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use a neutral voice instead if playful recasting feels shaming or agitating.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: EDIT THE FONT, NOT YOURSELF
rituals.goal: A thought displayed differently can be held differently.
rituals.steps:
1. Project — Project the sentence on an inner screen.
2. Shrink — Shrink it to caption size.
3. Move Metres — Move it two metres away.
4. Lower Opacity — Lower opacity, swap the heavy typeface for something ordinary, and place generous blank space around it.
5. Read Version — Read the edited version once, then look at real text nearby.
rituals.win: ✓ The thought changed format, and some of its spell broke.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Read Version”; loosen the label.
• Skip replay; use “Move Metres”.
• “Lower Opacity” — the rule loosened.
• At “Read Version”, compare “Project”.
• I can use “Shrink” without becoming the label.
rituals.formula_flow: Project → Shrink → Move Metres → Lower Opacity → Read Version
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Return to external grounding if visual manipulation feels unreal or disorienting.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: RETURN WITHOUT A TRIAL
rituals.goal: Drift needs a direction change, not a prosecution.
rituals.steps:
1. State Off — State what moved off course in plain language.
2. Delete Adjectives — Remove every adjective about your character.
3. Name Value — Name the value still available, then take the smallest move that serves it now.
4. Check After — Only after moving, decide whether the plan itself needs repair.
5. Skip Verdict — Re-enter the plan without putting yourself on trial.
rituals.win: ✓ Re-entry happened without opening a courtroom.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Skip Verdict”; keep the compass.
• Restart detected: “Name Value”.
• “Check After” keeps meaning in motion.
• Compare “State Off” with “Skip Verdict”.
• I can use “Delete Adjectives” while pain stays real.
rituals.formula_flow: State Off → Delete → Name Value → Move Whether → Skip Verdict
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Address repeated harmful drift with accountability and support, not endless self-restarts.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: TENSION’S EXIT PARTNER
rituals.goal: Teach one muscle where release lives.
rituals.steps:
1. Select Safe — Select a safe body region.
2. Tighten — Tighten it lightly—not maximally—during an easy inhale.
3. Leave Muscle — As air leaves, let the muscle become heavy and wide.
4. Compare After — Compare before and after, then move to a second region only if the first fully released.
5. End Clean — One clean contrast is enough.
rituals.win: ✓ I felt one clean contrast and stopped before turning it into a test.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “End Clean”; no breath-holding.
• Skip replay; use “Leave Muscle”.
• “Compare After” — alarm isn’t command.
• What lost power: “Select Safe” → “End Clean”?
• I can use “Tighten” while alarm rises.
rituals.formula_flow: Select Safe → Tighten → Leave Muscle → Compare After → End Clean
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Avoid injured, painful, recently operated, or cramping areas.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: FIVE SAFE SIGNALS
rituals.goal: Send calm through more than one doorway.
rituals.steps:
1. Build Sensory — Build a sensory sequence from what is available: one pleasing sight, steady sound, comforting texture, mild scent, and nourishing taste.
2. Receive Instead — Spend a few seconds receiving each instead of rushing to the next cue.
3. End Sense — End on the sense that feels most trustworthy today.
rituals.win: ✓ The clock stopped voting louder than the facts.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “End Sense”; slow the clock.
• Return once to “Receive Instead”.
• “Receive Instead” puts facts above speed.
• Difference check: “Build Sensory” → “End Sense”.
• I can use “Receive Instead” without rushing.
rituals.formula_flow: Build Sensory → Receive Instead → End Sense
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Avoid allergens, unsafe temperatures, substance triggers, or sensory input that overwhelms.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: DROP THE APPEAL
rituals.goal: Reality has already entered the room; the appeal is only in your mind.
rituals.steps:
1. State Fact — State the fact in plain past or present tense.
2. Remove Approval — Remove approval, blame, and every ‘should not have happened.’ Notice the body’s protest and answer, ‘Not liking it is allowed.
3. Add Nothing — Refusing its existence adds nothing.’ Choose the next response available in the world that actually exists.
rituals.win: ✓ I stopped appealing reality and moved inside the version that exists.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Add Nothing”; release extra blame.
• On return: “Remove Approval”.
• “Remove Approval” keeps blame in proportion.
• “Add Nothing”: what changed from “State Fact”?
• I can use “Remove Approval” without owning everything.
rituals.formula_flow: State Fact → Remove Approval → Add Nothing
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Acceptance must never be used to legitimise abuse, injustice, or preventable harm.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: TURN AGAIN
rituals.goal: Acceptance is often a direction repeated, not a mood achieved.
rituals.steps:
1. Catch Mind — Catch the mind reopening the case against what has already occurred.
2. Name Refusal — Name the refusal without criticism.
3. Rotate Attention — Rotate attention toward the existing fact and the action now possible.
4. Return Wheel — Each return is one turn of the wheel; stop counting after the chosen behaviour begins.
rituals.win: ✓ I turned back toward reality once more—and stopped counting when action began.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Return Wheel”; drop the scoreboard.
• Catch restart with “Rotate Attention”.
• “Rotate Attention” keeps worth off scoreboards.
• What changed: “Catch Mind” → “Return Wheel”?
• I can use “Name Refusal” without ranking my worth.
rituals.formula_flow: Catch Mind → Name Refusal → Rotate Attention → Return Wheel
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
If repeated turning becomes compulsive, step away and use ordinary support.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: PUT GOOD ON THE CALENDAR
rituals.goal: Positive events need appointments, not vague hope.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Genuinely — Choose one really reinforcing experience; assign it a time, place, and first action.
2. Protect Appointment — Protect the appointment from unnecessary multitasking.
3. Details — While it happens, notice three details worth encoding.
4. Lock It In — Afterward, resist grading whether you enjoyed it ‘enough.’
rituals.win: ✓ Good got a place on the calendar without needing a score.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Lock It In”; let feeling settle.
• On return: “Details”.
• “Details” separates feeling from fact.
• “Choose Genuinely” versus “Lock It In”: what eased?
• I can use “Protect Appointment” while emotion stays loud.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Genuinely → Protect Appointment → Details → Lock It In
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not force pleasure during grief or depression; attendance itself can be the result.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: BORROW THE SENSATION
rituals.goal: Teach the body that a safe signal is not the worst-case story.
rituals.steps:
1. Select Medically — Select a medically safe exercise that creates a mild feared sensation—brief spinning, stair walking, or breathing through a narrow straw only when appropriate.
2. Test Sensation — Predict what will happen, induce the sensation briefly, and observe recovery without usual calming it.
rituals.win: ✓ I predicted the sensation, borrowed it briefly, and watched my body recover.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Test Sensation”; no forcing.
• On return: “Test Sensation”.
• “Select Medically” keeps sensation as data.
• “Select Medically” → “Test Sensation”: what changed?
• I can use “Test Sensation” while sensation stays.
rituals.formula_flow: Select Medically → Test Sensation
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Obtain professional and medical guidance before body-sensation exposure, especially with health conditions.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: DESIGN THE SURPRISE
rituals.goal: A practice round works when reality breaks the prediction.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture Strongest — Picture the strongest testable prediction in visible terms.
2. Build Safe — Build a safe practice round aimed at that exact claim, not merely at feeling anxious.
3. Picture Outcome — Afterward, keep the original prediction, what occurred, and what the old model cannot easily explain.
rituals.win: ✓ What I feel and what is true are separate lanes again.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Picture Outcome”; let feeling settle.
• Return once to “Build Safe”.
• “Build Safe” separates feeling from fact.
• Look back: “Picture Strongest” → “Picture Outcome”.
• I can use “Build Safe” while emotion stays loud.
rituals.formula_flow: Picture Strongest → Build Safe → Picture Outcome
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Redesign rather than intensify when the test cannot fairly evaluate the belief.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: PENDULUM BETWEEN TWO TRUTHS
rituals.goal: Regulation can be built by travelling, not staying still.
rituals.steps:
1. Find Activated — Find one activated region and another settled or supported area.
2. Move Resource — Touch the difficult region with attention for a few seconds, then move to the resource.
3. Travel — Travel back and forth at a pace that preserves choice.
4. Finish Whichever — Finish on whichever location offers steadier awareness of your location.
rituals.win: ✓ Certainty remained unavailable; movement did not.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Finish Whichever”; leave it unanswered.
• If it flares, choose “Travel”.
• “Travel” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• “Find Activated” versus “Finish Whichever”: what eased?
• I can use “Move Resource” without a guarantee.
rituals.formula_flow: Find Activated → Move Resource → Travel → Finish Whichever
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop crossing if each visit amplifies distress rather than returning balance.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: WAIT FOR THE WHOLE BODY ANSWER
rituals.goal: Some experience forms before it can be explained.
rituals.steps:
1. Bring Mind — Bring the issue to mind lightly, then pause verbal analysis.
2. Ask Body — Ask the body, ‘What is the whole of this like?’ Wait for an image, phrase, posture, or global texture.
3. Check Whether — Check whether it fits by noticing a small inner yes, no, or shift.
4. Leave It Raw — Leave the answer unpolished.
rituals.win: ✓ The body answered before language polished it.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Leave It Raw”; leave it unanswered.
• If it flares, choose “Check Whether”.
• “Check Whether” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• “Leave It Raw”: what changed from “Bring Mind”?
• I can use “Ask Body” without a guarantee.
rituals.formula_flow: Bring Mind → Ask Body → Check Whether → Leave It Raw
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
End the inquiry if bodily attention creates panic, numbness, or feeling unreal or disconnected.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: COMPLETE THE DEFENCE IN MINIATURE
rituals.goal: An interrupted protective move may still be waiting.
rituals.steps:
1. Small — Notice the small impulse to push, turn, step back, shield, or say no.
2. Let Unfold — In a safe space, let it unfold slowly at ten percent strength.
3. Stop Completion — Stop at the natural completion and return to neutral posture.
4. Observe Whether — Observe whether the body receives an ending.
rituals.win: ✓ The urge peaked without becoming a contract.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Observe Whether”; let wanting crest.
• Use “Stop Completion” on return.
• “Stop Completion” keeps wanting off controls.
• “Observe Whether”: what changed from “Small”?
• I can use “Let Unfold” without obeying the urge.
rituals.formula_flow: Small → Let Unfold → Stop Completion → Observe Whether
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Never direct movement toward a person or continue if aggression escalates.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: FIND THE BODY’S WORKABLE DISTANCE
rituals.goal: Boundaries can be measured before they are argued.
rituals.steps:
1. Use Object — Using an object, doorway, or trusted person with consent, test near and far in small increments.
2. Breath — Notice breath, posture, urge, and clarity at each point.
3. Body — Notice where the body can stay present and communicate.
4. Set Workable Distance — That distance is data, not a permanent verdict.
rituals.win: ✓ The body found a workable distance without turning it into a verdict.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Set Workable Distance”; let wanting crest.
• Re-entry move: “Body”.
• “Body” keeps wanting off controls.
• “Set Workable Distance”: what changed from “Use Object”?
• I can use “Breath” without obeying the urge.
rituals.formula_flow: Use Object → Breath → Body → Set Workable Distance
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop immediately if consent changes or the exercise feels threatening.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: BORROW THE FLOOR
rituals.goal: Let external support do part of the holding.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Contact — Choose one contact point—feet, seat, back, forearms, or hands.
2. Release Extra — Increase pressure slightly, then release extra effort and notice what the surface continues to carry.
3. Name Texture — Name its texture, temperature, and steadiness.
4. Trust Ground — You need not manufacture a sense of ground.
rituals.win: ✓ The present regained enough detail to hold me.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Trust Ground”; notice the room.
• On return: “Name Texture”.
• “Name Texture” proves the present returned.
• At “Trust Ground”, compare “Choose Contact”.
• I can use “Release Extra” to return here.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Contact → Release Extra → Name Texture → Trust Ground
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Change position if pressure causes pain, numbness, or restricted circulation.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: CATCH THE RECOVERY SIGNAL
rituals.goal: Settling deserves as much attention as alarm.
rituals.steps:
1. Watch Swallow — After body alarm, watch for a swallow, sigh, warmth, trembling, yawn, moisture in the eyes, breath shift, or muscle release.
2. Name Accurately — When one appears, name it accurately and stay with its after-effect.
3. No Extra Trigger — Do not provoke more.
4. Look Like — Teach the mind what recovery looks like.
rituals.win: ✓ The alarm stayed loud, but the world got wider.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Look Like”; leave it unanswered.
• Restart detected: “No Extra Trigger”.
• “No Extra Trigger” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• “Watch Swallow” versus “Look Like”: what eased?
• I can use “Name Accurately” without a guarantee.
rituals.formula_flow: Watch Swallow → Name Accurately → No Extra Trigger → Look Like
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Seek care if shaking, breathing changes, or other symptoms seem medically concerning.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: CLOSE THE BODY FILE
rituals.goal: Do not close the file while the body is still asking for attention.
rituals.steps:
1. Scan Head — Scan from head to feet for remaining body alarm.
2. Select Strongest — Select the strongest residue and give it one stabilising response: support, movement, warmth, grounding in the present, or rest.
3. Rescan — Rescan only once.
4. State Today — State what is complete today and what belongs to later care.
rituals.win: ✓ Sensation became data instead of a verdict.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “State Today”; orient to now.
• Pulled back? Touch “Rescan”.
• “Rescan” moves memory toward then.
• Look back: “Scan Head” → “State Today”.
• I can use “Select Strongest” while staying in now.
rituals.formula_flow: Scan Head → Select Strongest → Rescan → State Today
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Seek help if the scan uncovers severe symptoms or increasing destabilisation.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: FIND THE BUSY HALF
rituals.goal: Not every unsettled breath needs a longer exhale.
rituals.steps:
1. Observe Ordinary — Observe three ordinary cycles.
2. Rate Inhale — Rate inhale effort and exhale release separately.
3. Phase — Which phase is working too hard?
4. Leave Timing — Ease only that side toward neutral—less pulling in or less pushing out—while leaving timing alone.
5. Check Whether — Check if urgency changes when imbalance decreases.
rituals.win: ✓ Comparison lost its right to set my value.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Check Whether”; drop the scoreboard.
• Re-entry move: “Phase”.
• “Leave Timing” keeps worth off scoreboards.
• Compare “Observe Ordinary” with “Check Whether”.
• I can use “Rate Inhale” without ranking my worth.
rituals.formula_flow: Observe Ordinary → Rate Inhale → Phase → Leave Timing → Check Whether
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop adjustment at the first sign of dizziness, strain, or breath fixation.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: ALTERNATE THE AIRWAY
rituals.goal: Move attention left and right until state feels organised.
rituals.steps:
1. Sit Easy — Sit comfortably.
2. Close Nostril — Without force, close one nostril and breathe through the other; switch sides for the next gentle cycle.
3. Continue Unhurried — Continue alternating with an unhurried hand.
4. Keep Breath — Keep the breath quiet and abandon retention.
5. Open Both Sides — Finish with both sides open and let breathing return to normal.
rituals.win: ✓ Left, right, centre: attention finished organised and unforced.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Open Both Sides”; no forcing.
• Use “Continue Unhurried” on return.
• “Keep Breath” keeps sensation as data.
• “Sit Easy” → “Open Both Sides”: what changed?
• I can use “Close Nostril” while sensation stays.
rituals.formula_flow: Sit Easy → Close Nostril → Continue Unhurried → Keep Breath → Open Both Sides
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Skip when congested, dizzy, breath-sensitive, or advised against the practice.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: VIBRATION ON THE WAY OUT
rituals.goal: Let sound carry the exhale without squeezing it.
rituals.steps:
1. Take Ordinary — Take an ordinary inhale.
2. Leave Feeling — Hum at a soft, comfortable pitch as air leaves, feeling vibration in lips, face, or chest.
3. Stop Empty — Stop before empty.
4. Listen Silence — Listen to the silence after the hum, then decide whether another round would still feel kind.
rituals.win: ✓ The current moment has edges again.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Listen Silence”; then keep moving.
• Loop back? Use “Stop Empty”.
• “Stop Empty” proves motion is available.
• At “Listen Silence”, compare “Take Ordinary”.
• I can use “Leave Feeling” before motivation.
rituals.formula_flow: Take Ordinary → Leave Feeling → Stop Empty → Listen Silence
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Cease with pain, coughing, light-headedness, or vocal discomfort.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: COOL AIR, WARM DECISION
rituals.goal: Borrow a settling cue from temperature.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine Mild — Shape the lips or tongue only if comfortable, notice a mild stream of cool air, and let exhalation leave naturally through the nose.
2. Coolness — Notice coolness rather than volume.
3. End After — Stop after a few easy cycles and choose one unhurried action.
rituals.win: ✓ Cooling changed the body volume before the mind wrote the explanation.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “End After”; notice the room.
• Shortcut: “Coolness”, once.
• “Coolness” proves the present returned.
• “Imagine Mild” → “End After”: what changed?
• I can use “Coolness” to return here.
rituals.formula_flow: Imagine Mild → Coolness → End After
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Avoid in cold sensitivity, unsuitable weather, breathing conditions, or discomfort.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE RETURN REP
rituals.goal: Attention strengthens on the comeback, not the stay.
rituals.steps:
1. Select Neutral — Select one neutral anchor.
2. Attention — Each time distraction appears, notice where attention went and escort it back without commentary.
3. Count Rather — Count returns rather than uninterrupted seconds.
4. End After — Finish after ten honest comebacks, even if focus never felt perfect.
rituals.win: ✓ Ten returns happened. Perfect focus was never required.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “End After”; release the score.
• Skip replay; use “Count Rather”.
• “Count Rather” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• Look back: “Select Neutral” → “End After”.
• I can use “Attention” without perfecting.
rituals.formula_flow: Select Neutral → Attention → Count Rather → End After
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Choose a broader practice if narrow focus increases agitation.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: LET DARKNESS BE COMPLETE
rituals.goal: Visual absence does not need a replacement image.
rituals.steps:
1. Set Darkness — In a safe darkened setting, notice darkness as the actual visual field.
2. Return Unfilled — When the mind manufactures shapes or stories, recognise image production and return to the unfilled field.
3. Stay Briefly — Stay briefly, then reintroduce light on purpose.
rituals.win: ✓ Darkness stayed complete for a moment; light returned by choice.
rituals.supports:
• One exhale after “Stay Briefly”; redirect attention.
• If it flares, choose “Return Unfilled”.
• “Return Unfilled” proves one signal leads.
• “Set Darkness” → “Stay Briefly”: what changed?
• I can use “Return Unfilled” amid noise.
rituals.formula_flow: Set Darkness → Return Unfilled → Stay Briefly
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Avoid this practice if darkness triggers panic, trauma, or perceptual disturbance.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: BEFORE THE SENTENCE
rituals.goal: Look for thought at the moment of assembly.
rituals.steps:
1. Hold Attention — Hold attention quietly and wait.
2. Earliest — When a thought begins, notice its earliest form: pressure, fragment, image, word, or felt orientation in space.
3. No Backtracking — Do not chase backward after it fully forms.
4. Catch the Birth — Simply Notice ‘birth’ and let the completed thought continue.
rituals.win: ✓ I caught the instant before the sentence became a story.
rituals.supports:
• One exhale after “Catch the Birth”; redirect attention.
• Return once to “No Backtracking”.
• “No Backtracking” proves one signal leads.
• Look back: “Hold Attention” → “Catch the Birth”.
• I can use “Earliest” amid noise.
rituals.formula_flow: Hold Attention → Earliest → No Backtracking → Catch the Birth
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Choose a visible anchor when vigilant waiting increases tension.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: FOLLOW IT TO ZERO
rituals.goal: A thought’s disappearance is usually ignored.
rituals.steps:
1. Select Naturally — Select one naturally occurring thought.
2. Stay Wording — Stay with its exact wording or image as it alters, fragments, loses relevance, or is replaced.
3. Identify Instant — Spot the first instant when no trace can be found.
4. Let It End — Do not resurrect it to verify the ending.
rituals.win: ✓ The thought ended. I did not drag it back for an encore.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Let It End”; loosen the label.
• Return once to “Identify Instant”.
• “Identify Instant” — the rule loosened.
• “Select Naturally” → “Let It End”: what changed?
• I can use “Stay Wording” without becoming the label.
rituals.formula_flow: Select Naturally → Stay Wording → Identify Instant → Let It End
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
End observation if tracking becomes obsessive or exhausting.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE RETURN CHAIN
rituals.goal: Ongoing sense is built from linked renewals.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Attention — Choose one attentional act small enough to repeat daily.
2. Set Cue — Define its cue, duration, and one tiny restart signal.
3. Return Repetition — Each session begins with the final second of yesterday’s intention: ‘return again.’ Protect repetition from heroic increases.
4. Link the Return — A chain is made of modest links.
rituals.win: ✓ I built the return out of small links instead of one heroic comeback.
rituals.supports:
• One exhale after “Link the Return”; redirect attention.
• Return once to “Return Repetition”.
• “Return Repetition” proves one signal leads.
• Look back: “Choose Attention” → “Link the Return”.
• I can use “Set Cue” amid noise.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Attention → Set Cue → Return Repetition → Link the Return
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Reduce frequency if ongoing sense crowds out sleep, duties, or flexibility.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: RETURN THE OUTCOME
rituals.goal: Effort is yours; total control was never issued.
rituals.steps:
1. Name Action — Name the action within your responsibility.
2. Name Result — Name the result you cannot command.
3. Use Language — Offer the second to God, life, reality, community, or a principle larger than ego—using language authentic to you.
4. Return the Outcome — Then do the first with full care.
rituals.win: ✓ Gave the outcome back and kept the quality of my action.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Return the Outcome”; slow the clock.
• If it flares, choose “Use Language”.
• “Use Language” puts facts above speed.
• What changed: “Name Action” → “Return the Outcome”?
• I can use “Name Result” without rushing.
rituals.formula_flow: Name Action → Name Result → Use Language → Return the Outcome
rituals.safety:

rituals.title: DEMOTE THE HEADLINE EXPERIENCE
rituals.goal: Foreground and background can share equal status.
rituals.steps:
1. Hold Sensation — Hold the dominant sensation or thought with three background what you notices—one sound, one contact point, one visual feature.
2. Give Attention — For a contained interval, give all four equal attentional weight without imagining a separate watcher.
3. Demote the Headline — Notice how centrality changes.
rituals.win: ✓ Headline demoted. The background gets equal screen time now.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Demote the Headline”; watch the thought.
• Skip replay; use “Give Attention”.
• “Give Attention” proves thought is observable.
• Difference check: “Hold Sensation” → “Demote the Headline”.
• I can use “Give Attention” without obeying thought.
rituals.formula_flow: Hold Sensation → Give Attention → Demote the Headline
rituals.safety:
PAUSE

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.
